about: Every idea Daniel gave for Last Fire, and where it stands. The game shows this file (Esc, CHECKLIST). done = in the game and tested; in = in the game, not yet proven; next = being built now; later = agreed, not started; talk = still being discussed with him.

items.idea: Hyper-awareness
A villain who is iniquitous by nature
Random elements, dry dark humor, lots of mayhem
Hanging out with the guys, yet surviving alone in the dark
Maze Runner vibe, but not trapped: the maze is the obvious lore, so dark that people want to learn before entering
Who you are
items.where: undecided

items.idea: The origin is honestly unknown, like humanity's own
items.where: proposed: everyone remembers the same ordinary Tuesday, then the dark

items.idea: Trapped by need, not walls: a community bound to the fire, punishing anyone who doesn't contribute
items.where: his answer: the camp itself keeps the rules (people of the camp, not players), so it works alone or with friends. proposed: the fire is a commons; free riders are cut out of its light

items.idea: Light against dark (good vs evil frame), made interesting by the truth
The dark doesn't care: you're meaningless on its scale (entropy, not malice)
The game tells the truth: statistically, winning is never on your side
items.where: proposed: decay, diminishing returns, no forever-win; the score is how long you hold

items.idea: Teaches entropy, diminishing returns, scale, existential dread, logic, suspense, psychological payoff
Feeling real matters more than being real
The mirror realm: the most stereotypical day on Earth, flipped only where it's cool
items.where: proposed: commute into the dark, shifts at the fire, a school for the maze, smiling signs

items.idea: Community life: work, fire dues, chores; what you get follows what you contribute
Soft punishment for never feeding the fire: no more lanterns, higher prices, lower morale; no forced rule, 'we know'
Optional jobs for better gear and convenience; honest work only, never exploitable; all measured and logged
Contribution is credit the camp remembers (the lone wolf who did his part is welcome back)
Grinding while friends are offline has a measured low impact, so nobody gets outscaled
items.where: proposal: offline work mostly builds the shared camp; the absent friend's share waits

items.idea: Every layer min-maxed by the simulators (prices, morale, dues)
A NOTE button to give feedback while playing (like Era 1)
items.where: Tab, then TALK or type, then SEND TO CLAUDE (a picture of the moment goes with it)

items.idea: Lore first, then merge it with the mechanics: each relies on the other

items.idea: Updates arrive while I play: a pop-up, yes or no, and it feels automatic (straight back where I was)
